NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
What is being proposed: A multi-layered bearing pad with sacrificial ozone-resistant elastomer layers and distributed strain-limiting mesh reinforcement between elastomer layers. Standard practice uses homogeneous elastomer layers with uniform reinforcement throughout, which provides no targeted protection against localized creep or ozone attack. This intervention creates a self-healing mechanical architecture where sacrificial layers absorb environmental degradation while the strain-limiting mesh prevents excessive creep deformation in the primary structural layers. The closest existing practice is multi-layer elastomer bearings with different hardness layers, but those do not incorporate sacrificial protection zones or distributed strain limiting. This mechanism attacks the failure by containing degradation to sacrificial layers while mechanically constraining the primary layers from excessive creep.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing relation for creep strain in elastomers is ε_creep = σ·t·C, where σ is stress, t is time, and C is creep compliance. The strain-limiting mesh reduces effective stress in primary layers by redistributing load: σ_primary = σ_applied·(A_sacrificial/A_total), where A_sacrificial is the area of sacrificial layers. For a 3-layer design with 30% sacrificial layers, σ_primary is reduced by 30%, directly reducing creep strain by 30% over time. The sacrificial layers contain antioxidants and ozone-resistant compounds that deplete at a calibrated rate, protecting the primary layers for the 75-year service life while sacrificial layers degrade predictably.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Components: 
- Primary structural layers: Chloroprene rubber (Neoprene) with 20% glass fiber mesh reinforcement
- Sacrificial layers: Polychloroprene with 30% higher carbon black content and additional antioxidants ( procurable from specialty rubber suppliers)
- Strain-limiting mesh: 304 stainless steel wire mesh (3mm grid, 0.5mm wire diameter, procurable from industrial suppliers)
- Bonding layers: Chlorinated polyethylene adhesive (procurable from adhesive suppliers)
- Installation procedure: Clean bearing surfaces, apply adhesive in alternating pattern, layer components under controlled pressure (15 kN/m²), cure at 25°C for 72 hours
- Required development: Calibration of sacrificial layer depletion rate through accelerated aging tests to match 75-year service life

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Installability: Comparable to standard practice - same number of layers, same bonding procedure, same curing requirements
- Operability: Identical - no change in operational parameters or monitoring requirements
- Maintenance: Same - no additional maintenance procedures beyond standard inspection
- Cost: 15-20% higher material cost due to additional materials and manufacturing complexity, offset by extended service life and replacement cost avoidance
- Deployment burden: Same installation timeline, same equipment requirements, same skill level needed for installation

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Subject test bearings to accelerated aging (40°C, 100% ozone concentration) while applying cyclic load (5 Hz, 0-10 MPa stress) for 6 months (equivalent to 75 years of service). Measure vertical deflection drift weekly using LVDTs with 0.01mm resolution. Pass/fail threshold: deflection drift must remain below 10% of initial deflection after 6 months of testing. Kill criterion: If deflection drift exceeds 10% at any point, the test fails and the design is falsified. Control group: Standard homogeneous bearing pad tested under identical conditions. Test requires 5 samples to account for variability.
